chapter: Ben Webster, Tatum and Los Angeles scene
title: Ellington in Seattle: Ben Webster, Blanton, Strayhorn and stride piano
summary: When Ellington played Seattle, he became close to Ben Webster, played with Blanton, and Ben introduced him to stride pianists.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Because they were gonna go someplace after work and play, and they'd say, "How about going down to the Green Lantern or the so-and-so?" I'd say, "Well, I'm gonna be there, and I want to play for you." And I played for Joe Thomas, I wound up... They were there for about three days, and I played for him every night. I played for Dan Grissom while he was singing. And I learned all their arrangements.

And then Ellington came for two weeks, and that's when I got firmly in there with Ben, you know -- he and I just turned into brothers right there. That was all day and all night, just the two of us playing. We'd hook up with a drummer or a bass player or somethin' like that, and play. And I played a lot with Jimmy Blanton. And I met Strayhorn; he had just joined. And Ray Nance...
Yeah, '38, '39... [RAY NANCE JOINED DUKE IN NOV. '40] Because I had already known Ben... I had been corresponding with him for years, though, before I came to California.

Oh yeah! He could stride like crazy. He was a Stride piano player. Yeah, once he got all warmed up, he'd go... He got me all acquainted with James P. Johnson, that's all he would listen to. You know, Fats and Donald
Lambert, Willie the Lion... He introduced me to Willie the Lion..
Where did you meet the Lion?
Out on Broadway. [CHUCKLES] He introduced me to Buddy Tate. He introduced me to everybody. He used to take me around with him just like a dog.
